name: Ariad Two-Servo Robot — Component-First Rev A
purpose: A serviceable two-servo embodied-AI robot enclosure designed from selected Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W and Feetech SCS0009 hardware envelopes outward.

parts.name: Front body shell
parts.role: Protect the selected hardware layout and establish camera, servo-axis, tray-latch, ventilation, and rear-service boundaries.
parts.notes: The larger shell is derived from the internal Pi and dual-servo arrangement; external proportions are secondary to component access.

parts.name: Servo chassis and electronics tray
parts.role: Carry structural loads, capture both SCS0009 body envelopes, slide into the shell, and support the removable Pi carrier.
parts.notes: Integrated servo cradle lips are provisional until the purchased servo cases are measured and insertion force is tested.

parts.name: Tether-ready service panel
parts.role: Provide tool-less rear access and a bounded opening for the regulated 5 V Rev A power lead.
parts.notes: Rev A intentionally excludes a battery and charging circuit.

parts.name: Left rotating limb
parts.role: Provide a long rounded ground-contact surface through the left servo rotation envelope.
parts.notes: Printed flat; recovery, gait, load capacity, and collision freedom remain unverified.

parts.name: Right rotating limb
parts.role: Provide a long rounded ground-contact surface through the right servo rotation envelope.
parts.notes: Mirrored role; recovery, gait, load capacity, and collision freedom remain unverified.

parts.name: Left keyed servo adapter
parts.role: Connect the selected servo horn family to the left printed limb through a replaceable keyed interface.
parts.notes: The supplied horn and center screw remain purchased hardware; exact spline and horn fit require the physical servo.

parts.name: Right keyed servo adapter
parts.role: Connect the selected servo horn family to the right printed limb through a replaceable keyed interface.
parts.notes: The supplied horn and center screw remain purchased hardware; exact spline and horn fit require the physical servo.

parts.name: Camera bezel and locating frame
parts.role: Locate a 25 x 24 mm OV5647-family reservation against the front shell while keeping the lens field unobstructed.
parts.notes: Supplier-specific PCB, lens, cable, and hole positions must be measured before claiming fit.

parts.name: Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W carrier
parts.role: Slide onto the chassis and provide four standoffs using the official 58 x 23 mm Zero-family mounting-hole pattern.
parts.notes: M2.5 nylon fasteners are intentionally used for the purchased PCB; printed-part joins remain tool-less.

component_envelopes.name: Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W
component_envelopes.source: Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W official product brief and mechanical drawing: 65 x 30 mm outline and 58 x 23 mm mounting pattern; connector and fitted-header keep-outs remain configuration-dependent.

component_envelopes.name: Feetech SCS0009 serial bus servo
component_envelopes.source: Feetech SCS0009 product specification; 20T horn/spline revision and supplied horn geometry must be checked on the purchased unit.

component_envelopes.name: OV5647-family Pi Zero camera module
component_envelopes.source: GrowBot V0 selects an OV5647 camera; the Ariad reservation accepts a common 25 x 24 mm board envelope, but the exact supplier board, lens, and narrow CSI cable are not selected.

component_envelopes.name: MPU-6050 GY-521 IMU module
component_envelopes.source: Functional reservation only; GY-521 supplier layouts vary and no mounting interface is released until a board is selected and measured.

interfaces.name: Snap-latched shell to structural tray
requirements: Tray slides from the rear and both planar hooks remain externally releasable.
Servo loads route through the tray and shell, never through the Pi.
Fit and latch life require physical calibration.

interfaces.name: Slide-lock rear service panel
requirements: Panel remains removable with the power disconnected.
The tether notch must not pinch the selected cable.
No battery or charger is enclosed in Rev A.

interfaces.name: Left servo-to-limb rotary joint
interfaces.axis: Shared transverse X axis through the left body wall
requirements: Limb sweep must not collide with the body shell.
Manufacturer horn hardware may be used.

interfaces.name: Right servo-to-limb rotary joint
interfaces.axis: Shared transverse X axis through the right body wall
requirements: Limb sweep must not collide with the body shell.
Manufacturer horn hardware may be used.

interfaces.name: Camera board and bezel stack
requirements: The PCB, lens, and CSI ribbon must not be compressed.
Supplier-specific dimensions must replace the reservation before fit is claimed.

interfaces.name: Pi carrier to chassis and board
requirements: The Pi uses four M2.5 nylon fasteners at the 58 x 23 mm pattern.
microSD, USB, GPIO, CSI ribbon, and ventilation remain serviceable.

interfaces.name: Dual servo cradle capture
requirements: Both servo bodies are supported against reaction torque.
Servo wires exit without sharp bends.
Insertion and retention forces require measured hardware and physical testing.

assembly_constraints: Component selection and internal layout precede the exterior blueprint and shell release.
Rev A contains no battery or charging module and uses an external regulated 5 V supply.
Exactly two independently actuated limbs are mounted outside the left and right body walls.
No structural load routes through the camera, IMU, or compute board.
Separately printed parts use serviceable slide, snap, press, or keyed interfaces; purchased electronics may use manufacturer-appropriate fasteners.
Every printed part receives its own geometry, orientation, slice, and artifact records.
Hardware remains disconnected and physical success remains unclaimed.
unresolved_questions: Which exact OV5647 camera board and narrow CSI ribbon will replace the camera reservation?
Which exact GY-521 module will define the IMU mount?
What are the measured supplied-horn and spline dimensions of the purchased SCS0009 revision?
Which regulated external 5 V supply and cable overmould define the tether keep-out?
What measured clearance coupon maps the 0.4 mm interlock allowance to the eventual printer and PETG batch?
What mass distribution and limb profile are required for simulated and physical recovery?
claim_boundary: This component-first Rev A uses manufacturer-sourced Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W board/mounting dimensions and Feetech SCS0009 body envelopes. The camera and IMU remain supplier-dependent reservations. Prototype CAD and disconnected slicing do not prove purchased-component fit, horn fit, interlock fit, latch life, collision freedom, balance, motion, electrical safety, thermal behavior, or physical success.
